the_finding_i_am_fixing: game/src/world/province.js draws no settlement buildings at all. 202 buildings across 8 settlements reach a door table and a .length and nothing else. VP04-settlement-street photographs terrain. The 50 townspeople round 2 put outdoors at 09:00 stand on a bare pad.

reconnaissance.kit_gap: Each settlement's architecture_kit.meshes declares 8-10 ids (RI-WLD03 R5 requires >=8 bespoke building meshes). render/interior.js implements exactly FOUR per town — the four that appear in interior props[] — so 37 of the 69 declared kit meshes have no implementation anywhere. Those 37 are the EXTERIOR-only meshes.
reconnaissance.kit_is_a_town_property: Every interior in a town carries the same four tho_/arc_/hel_... ids, so 'a building's exterior kit matches its interior kit' is a per-town identity that must hold building by building.
reconnaissance.footprints: 112 of 202 buildings are kind:'interior' and their exterior footprint is declared at interiors/<id>.json continuity.exterior_footprint_m (12.4x14.4 .. 16x18). 34 sealed-with-reason and 56 structure have no declared footprint and must be derived by building_kind.
reconnaissance.placement_conflict: Declared footprints are larger than the plan's nearest-neighbour spacing in five of eight towns (archon nn 2.8 m against a 13.6 m footprint). Positions are RI-WLD03 R4's legibility proof and must NOT be moved; footprints will be shrunk deterministically only where one building would otherwise swallow another's centre, and the count reported.
reconnaissance.collision: sim.cell is EMPTY_CELL in the province, so stepWorldCollision() returns immediately and nothing in the open world is solid. The settlement collision set will be installed as sim.cell with sim.cellId left null, so province streaming, _settleWorld and groundInActiveCell are untouched.

Run the tool.

SECTIONS 5 AND 6 OF tools/world/w1-04-r3-exterior.mjs --live were never run to completion in that tool; I killed the run during section 5. Section 6's question was re-asked and PASSED by w1-04-r3-consume.mjs. Section 5's question is §C of the collision tool and is open (previous line).

THE FOOTPRINT / PLAN CONFLICT IS MITIGATED, NOT RESOLVED. Five of the eight town plans place buildings closer together than the interiors declare them to be wide (Archon: 2.8 m apart, 13.6 m across). I shrink, never move, because the positions are RI-WLD03 R4's legibility proof. Result: 71 of 202 drawn at exactly the declared exterior_footprint_m, 54 shrunk, and 12 pairs across Blackrose/Archon/Lilmoth/Soulrest still overlap by more than 45% of the smaller building because the 3.4 m minimum footprint stops the shrink. The right fix is in the DATA — either the settlement generator's offsets or the interiors' declared footprints — and it is not mine to make in this round.

A DEFECT IN interior.js FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED. `Object.assign(group, { position: ... })` in bla_prison_block, barrel_row and bench_pair throws every time (three's Object3D.position is not writable and the file is 'use strict'). buildInterior catches it per prop and silently substitutes fallbackProp WITHOUT incrementing props_fallback, so 34 prop instances across 22 rooms are drawing a generic crate while round 2's own summary counts them as built — and one of them, bla_prison_block, is a Blackrose architecture-kit mesh, so Blackrose draws 7 of its 8 declared kit ids and not 8. The fix is g.position.set(...) at interior.js:228, :272 and :374. I did not apply it because a critic is grading round 2 against that file right now and the instruction was to keep interior.js additive. Somebody should.

RI-WLD03 M13 (the blind top-down layout test) is now POSSIBLE for the first time — there is settlement geometry to render orthographically — and I did not run it. It is blind_pair: yes and RULES.md rule 25 forbids me judging a pack I built.
RI-WLD03 R2's back room, R3's faction-hall rivalry geometry and RI-WLD13 N7 (water) are untouched by this round.
The exterior draws no NPC, no sign, no street furniture and no ground surface change. A town is buildings on the region's own terrain; there is no paving, no market stall and no yard.
No timing figure is published anywhere in this piece, because the whole run was far above RULES.md rule 21's browser cap (RULES.md rule 26).

QUALITY, NOT CORRECTNESS: in the Helstrom shot several buildings read as open-topped crates, because a town's roof rule is drawn at the wall height and Helstrom's shell dome is narrower than its footprint, so the corners are open to the sky from above. Nothing measured here catches that — every count is a count — and it is the kind of defect only a picture finds. It wants a roof that covers the plan, and it is not fixed.

RULES.md rule 28 is listed as binding and says the orchestrator banks the tree, and here the two instructions collide concretely rather than formally: this change is only alive if game/src/render/interior.js, game/src/world/province.js, game/src/engine.js and game/src/harness/api.js are committed together with the new module, and at this moment three of those four also carry OTHER live agents' unfinished edits in the working tree — W1-READABLES has an unfinished readable-placement change sitting in interior.js right now, and engine.js and api.js are claimed by four more pieces. cross_piece_warning: STATED PLAINLY FOR THE PIECES THAT OWN THOSE SYSTEMS. sim.cell now holds real geometry while the player stands inside a town in the province, where it was EMPTY_CELL before. Four systems read sim.cell and every one of them changes behaviour there: the body's depenetration (sim/world-collision.js), the camera's spring arm (sim/camera.js — the arm can now be obstructed in a street), stealth line of sight (sim/stealth/perception.js — sim/stealth/system.js's hasGeometry now sees shapes in a town), and conjured walls (sim/magic/apply.js). This is deliberate: a second collision set would have given the right answer to one of them and left the other three walking through masonry. sim.cellId is still null in the province, so every camera-fixture measurement in the tree is untouched, and __w1_04_townSolids(false) removes the walls again for anyone who needs the old arm.
finding_vp04_camera_is_inside_a_building: THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS ROUND FOUND, and a critic should start here. VP04-settlement-street's declared camera pose [3825.5, 15.1, 879] is 3.8 m from the centre of thorn-sapwell and INSIDE its footprint. That was invisible while the town was a bare pad — the round-1 verdict photographed 'root arches, green slabs and fog' from that spot and called it terrain — and the moment the buildings exist the viewpoint is standing in one: the shot at that pose is now a dark frame of the inside of a wall. So VP04 has stopped being terrain, and what it has become is a picture of a building's interior surface, which is not what the viewpoint is for. Measured, not guessed: renderer-side, 15 of Thorn's 15 buildings are in the scene graph at that pose, all 15 are in front of the camera and 10 project inside the frame; offline, exterior.js#insideBuilding puts the camera inside thorn-sapwell. I did NOT move the viewpoint: tools/harness/viewpoints.json is not my file and HARNESS.md is explicit that changing a pose invalidates every cross-wave comparison that used it. Whoever owns it should move VP04 to a street rather than a shopfront — a 2.5 m-clear standing point 40 m out on Thorn's own plan, with 15 buildings in the forward cone, is [3856.5, _, 875.3] looking at [3820, _, 859]; tools/world/w1-04-r3-consume.mjs will photograph whatever pose it is given.

found_on_arrival: reports/w1-04-r3-collision.json EXISTS and is a COMPLETED run (all three sections, errors []), but it is not a usable measurement and I am not reporting its numbers. §A returns byte-identical with_walls and walls_cut on all 15 walks — an inert control arm, RULES.md rule 6 — and §B reports 0 of 15 solid on the wall in every town.

CAUSE 1 (inert control arm), in game/src/harness/api.js __w1_04_townSolids(on): it sets engine._townCell = null BEFORE calling engine._settleSettlementSolids(), and that method’s off-branch only clears sim.cell when it can still recognise it as _townCell (`if (this._townCell && this.sim.cell === this._townCell)`). With _townCell already nulled the branch is dead, sim.cell keeps the wall CollisionCell, and the walls were never removed. Both arms were the walls-on arm.

CAUSE 2 (§B reads 0 solid everywhere), in tools/world/w1-04-r3-collision.mjs: it samples solidAt at ABSOLUTE y = 1.0 m (`b.y === undefined ? gy : gy` is a no-op ternary that always yields 1.0). The wall slabs are boxes spanning groundY+offset .. +height, and Thorn stands at y≈15, Soulrest at y≈8. The probe was sampling underground.

CAUSE 3 (§A picked door sides), same tool: its comment says it approaches a wall that is NOT the doorway and the code never excludes entry_side, so 6 of the 15 walks walked in through the door and were scored as walking through a wall.
